name: Qwen2-VL: Enhancing Vision-Language Model's Perception of the World at Any Resolution
problem: A single 1-D RoPE position index cannot express the 2-D/3-D spatial structure of an image or video, and naive per-modality index assignment degrades cross-modal alignment - so a VLM cannot exploit high native resolution without losing accuracy on text.
mechanism: M-RoPE (Multimodal Rotary Position Embedding). Decompose the rotary embedding head_dim into three sections and assign each section a different position index: temporal for video frames, height for image rows, width for image columns (text reuses the temporal slot). Section sizes are per-model-config (Qwen2-VL ships mrope_section [16,24,24] for head_dim 64), and multimodal position ids are precomputed by a get_rope_index pass. Qwen2-VL itself is native-resolution: dynamic resolution tokenisation, no resizing or cropping to a fixed bucket.
speedup_reported: NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM. The abstract reports quality and capability results only: Qwen2-VL-72B achieves results comparable to GPT-4o and Claude3.5-Sonnet across multimodal benchmarks, scaling studied at 2B/8B/72B. No throughput, latency or memory figure. The serving-relevant consequence is architectural: M-RoPE's section split means the rotary computation is a per-section gather, so it must be implemented rather than assumed by a serving engine.
